title: 1. h4 vs. 2000 ELO Players on Chess.com
summary: Rated online blitz (3-min) on chess.com where the narrator (~2085) tries to climb to 2100 by always opening 1.h4 as White (and mirroring with ...h5 as Black) against ~2000-rated humans such as BIGGESTBAUCE (2033). Otherwise normal chess. Playable as a 'forced opening' challenge.
rules: Self-imposed: as White play 1.h4; as Black answer with 1...h5 (game 1 he had Black).

opponent.name: ~2000-rated humans (e.g. BIGGESTBAUCE 2033)
opponent.avatar_description: Generic chess.com avatars; thumbnail is a confused cat 'eh? 1.h4?'.

board.theme_notes: standard green chess.com board with 3-minute clocks.

setup: rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/7P/8/PPPPPPP1/RNBQKBNR b KQkq - 0 1 (after 1.h4) when White; when Black, mirror with ...h5.
current_impl_issues: Implemented as forced-opening 1.h4 vs 2000 bot - essentially correct. Could add 3+0 clock and the Black ...h5 mirror option.
evidence: Transcript 00:01 'climb my rating to 2100 by using the opening pawn to h4... game number one we actually get the black pieces, so I will just do the inverse and throw pawn to h5'; 01:45 'lost half of my time already'. Frames (visual_c): green board, 3-min clocks, BIGGESTBAUCE (2033), me 2085.
